review: 1:1 מִי יַגִּיד — 'who can tell', standing for the Arabic exclamation يَا تُرَى; a literal 'who, I wonder' has no biblical idiom, so the rhetorical question is used.
1:2 כְּגֹאֲלֵנוּ הֶחָבִיב — 'like our beloved Redeemer'; גֹּאֵל is the fixed biblical kinsman-redeemer word, and הֶחָבִיב is the hymn's name for Christ throughout this book.
2:8 עָלֵינוּ הַתְּפִלָּה — 'prayer is upon us' (i.e. it is ours to do), for فَعَلَيْنَا بِالصَّلَاة; the Hebrew prepositional phrase is the closest idiom.
3:6 מִנְּשֹׂא כֹּבֶד דְּאָגוֹת — 'from bearing the weight of cares'; the construct chain replaces the Arabic جَرَّا حَمْلِ الْهُمُوم without the extra syllables of a relative clause.
Each stanza is one printed 8-line block; Hebrew keeps the 8-line block so the tune's two halves stay intact.
